title: Stored Procedures (CREATE PROCEDURE) & Transaction Control
description: Compare Functions vs Stored Procedures (PG 11+) and control transactions inside procedures with COMMIT and ROLLBACK.

data.text: Before PostgreSQL 11, developers could only write Functions (`CREATE FUNCTION`). Functions execute within the caller's transaction and cannot commit or roll back. PostgreSQL 11 introduced true **Stored Procedures (`CREATE PROCEDURE`)**, which are invoked via `CALL` and can commit transactions internally.

rows: Cannot commit or roll back internally

data.title: Batch Deletion Procedure with Incremental Commits
data.content: Prevents lock accumulation on large tables by committing every 10,000 rows.

data.title: Key Takeaways
points: Use `CREATE PROCEDURE` when you need transaction control (`COMMIT`/`ROLLBACK`).
Stored procedures are executed using `CALL procedure_name()`.
Essential for long-running batch operations that need periodic checkpoint commits.
